subject: Reserved capacity: flexible term options & pricing sensitivity / approval path
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@skyline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skyline.ai>, DataOps Team <dataops@skyline.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity options — pricing sensitivity to GPU cost swings

Ben / team,

Thanks for the demo last week — Skyline is excited about the latency and cost profile Redwood showed. We're evaluating a reserved capacity commitment for our inference workloads (primarily 8k context Transformer family). Before we move deeper we'd like clarity on two things:

1) How do your reserved capacity discounts react if underlying GPU market prices move (indexation / pass-through mechanics)? Do you offer capped pass-throughs or triggers that limit downside risk for us?

2) What approval path is required for deeper discounts / longer tenors (>24 months, >25% discount)? We have an internal procurement threshold that requires CFO approval beyond certain discounts/commitments.

Scope: targeting 60-80 steady GPUs equivalent, with potential 2x burst for three months after launch. Looking for pricing scenarios for 12/24/36 month tenors plus a recommended contract language for a GPU-price contingency clause.

Can you send a few modeled scenarios and the internal approval path so we can align with procurement?

Best,
Evan Brooks
Head of Cloud & Platform
Skyline Analytics

--
Attachment: none (will accept an initial scenarios spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@skyline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity options — pricing sensitivity to GPU cost swings

Evan — thanks for the clear ask. We put together three scenario families and included the modeling in the attached spreadsheet (reserve-pricing-scenarios-v2.xlsx). Highlights up front:

- Tenors: 12 / 24 / 36 months. Deeper discounts at 24 and 36 months with volume tiers.
- Pass-through mechanics: we offer a market-indexed pass-through tied to a 30-day GPU index with a +/- floor/ceiling. Options: capped pass-through (we absorb up to X%), shared-index (50/50 movement), or full pass-through with cap. See sheet tab "index-options".
- Burst capacity: add-on burst lanes available as on-demand at a reduced short-term rate; recommend reserving base 1.5x steady to avoid throttling.
- Approval path (internal): Sales manager approval up to 20% list discount; Sales VP approval up to 35%; anything >35% requires Finance + GTM leadership sign-off and legal to sign special price contingencies. We can pre-approve a one-time executive approval slab for strategic customers.

Attached: scenario workbook and a draft term-sheet (PDF) that includes suggested GPU price contingency language (two variants: index-with-cap and index-trigger).

Next steps: if Skyline favors one of the scenarios, we'll route the target discount through finance for quick pre-approval and then surface to legal for the final redline. Recommend a 24-month capped-pass-through as a pragmatic middle ground.

Let me know if you'd like a call to walk through the workbook this week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity options — pricing sensitivity to GPU cost swings (Skyline)

Team — reviewed the workbook and the proposed options. Finance position and approval path:

- Approved commercial baseline: 24-month tenor with tiered volume discounts and a capped pass-through. We will absorb up to 8% adverse movement in the GPU index; customer absorbs movements beyond that up to a contract cap of 20% total pass-through in a 12-month window.
- Maximum negotiable discount to list before requiring exec sign-off: 30% (Sales VP + CFO). Any negotiated aggregate discount beyond 30% requires CEO sign-off.
- For 36-month proposals where the customer requests higher upfront discounts we require a quarterly true-up and a minimum annual usage guarantee.
- Revenue & billing: require clear billing callouts for index adjustments and a separate surcharge line on invoices to keep ARR clean. Legal to add index-trigger windows and a reporting cadence.

I'll approve routing to Legal to draft the final clause. Once legal has redlined, we'll prepare an exec packet if Skyline asks for >30% discount.
